_README: Real repo ids for the eval cases (evals/cases.jsonl). INTRANET-OWNED — fill these in on the box.
Why this file exists: RUNBOOK-65 caught the external side writing `mc-hk-hase-csl-sms-deli-job`
into a runbook AND into eval cases. It is not a real repo id. The system correctly fail-closed
(0 MCP calls, which is the guard working), but a question built on a repo that does not exist
tests nothing — and a BASELINE built on it would be worse than no baseline.
This is the same lesson as the four rounds before it: names, shapes, formats and values that
only the intranet can observe do not belong in external Python or external fixtures. Keep the
abstract side out here, let the box own every real name.
HOW TO FILL: run `python -m webapp.cli list_repos` (or the list_repos tool) and paste EXACT ids.
Any placeholder left empty makes its cases SKIP with a loud note — never run against a guess.
sms_delivery      : a repo that delivers SMS AND resolves to a LogDream app if possible
(RUNBOOK-62 measured 51/460 resolvable; prefer one of those 51)
push_delivery     : the equivalent on the push/Aurora lane
ingress           : the entry service (mc-hk-hase-ingress-api has been verified on the box
before, so it is pre-filled — correct it if that is wrong)
known_use_case    : a use-case id that EXISTS in the active snapshot
unknown_use_case  : a use-case-shaped id CONFIRMED ABSENT from every active snapshot table.
RUNBOOK-66: the first shipped default (K9999) turned out to be REAL, which
is why this now ships blank — verify absence, do not assume it.
vendor_repo       : a repo whose name contains a vendor token, for the do-not-infer-vendor case
